identity.name: gmail-apps-script-mail
identity.summary: Send mail and manage Gmail/Calendar through a Google Apps Script web app

handover.summary: Wraps a Google Apps Script web app that fronts Gmail and Calendar. Verified by calling whoami against the live endpoint: it answered as it@aljashtrading.com with 1485 of 1500 daily sends left. What bites: the Apps Script rejects application/json and answers with an HTML page, and each mailbox carries its own daily cap so a batch can die partway while another mailbox is fine. Both are recorded. Left undone: no retry or backoff, no batch send, and the quota check is advisory rather than enforced before a send.

capability.does: Sends email and manages Gmail threads, labels and Calendar events through a Google Apps Script web app fronted by a local CLI wrapper.

failureModes.symptom: The Apps Script returns an HTML error page or a redirect instead of JSON, and the caller fails to parse it.
failureModes.trigger: POSTing with Content-Type: application/json. The Apps Script web app only accepts text/plain and treats anything else as a form post.

resolution.change: The wrapper always sends Content-Type: text/plain with a JSON body.

failureModes.symptom: Sends start failing partway through a batch while a different mailbox still works.
failureModes.trigger: Each mailbox has its own daily cap: the agent mailbox allows 1500/day, the personal and techrealm mailboxes 100/day each.

resolution.workaround: Call quota before a batch and pick the mailbox with headroom via _endpoint.
resolution.residualRisk: A long batch can still exhaust a 100/day mailbox mid-run.

detail.rule: Pass "_endpoint":"personal" or "techrealm" to send as those addresses; omit it to use the default agent mailbox.
detail.rationale: The default is a shared operational mailbox with a much larger quota, so mail meant to look personal must say so explicitly or it goes out as the agent.

integration.title: Pass the payload as one single-quoted JSON argument

detail.rule: Every action takes exactly one argument: a JSON object quoted as a single shell arg, with inner quotes escaped.
detail.rationale: Splitting the payload across shell words silently drops fields, which looks like the API ignoring them.

environment.name: MAILCLI_PATH
environment.purpose: Path to the local wrapper that holds the Apps Script URL and API key.

environment.name: MAIL_APPS_SCRIPT_URL
environment.purpose: The Apps Script /exec web app URL the wrapper POSTs to.

environment.name: MAIL_APPS_SCRIPT_API_KEY
environment.purpose: Shared key sent in the POST body as apiKey. Held by the wrapper; never passed on the command line.

exports.name: install
exports.summary: Replace with what this pack actually exports.

healthcheck.description: Prints the effective mailbox and remaining daily quota.

network.purpose: POST the action payload to the Apps Script web app.

secrets.name: MAIL_APPS_SCRIPT_API_KEY
secrets.purpose: Authenticates the caller to the Apps Script.

integration.prompt:
Send mail or manage Gmail/Calendar through the local wrapper.

One argument, always: a JSON object as a single quoted shell arg.

  python3 $MAILCLI_PATH sendEmail '{"to":"a@b.com","subject":"S","body":"B"}'

Mailboxes: omit _endpoint for the default agent mailbox (1500/day); "_endpoint":"personal" or "_endpoint":"techrealm" for those addresses (100/day each). Call whoami to see which mailbox you are, and quota before any batch — the small mailboxes run out mid-run and the failure is easy to miss.

Other actions take the same shape: whoami, quota, searchThreads, getThread, replyToThread, label operations, createEvent, findEvents.

The Apps Script URL and API key live in the wrapper. Do not pass them on the command line and do not copy them into the repository.
